chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Bureyd al-Ajaly, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a believer who killed a man known for Nasb (hostility to the Imams) upon his religion, out of anger for Allah, Blessed and High. Would he be killed for it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for them (the rulers/judges), they would kill him for it. But if it were raised to a Just, apparent Imam, he would not kill him for it.' I said, 'So his blood would be invalidated (no diya)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but if he has inheritors, then it is upon the Imam to give them the diya (blood money) from the public treasury (Bayt al-Mal), because his killer killed him out of anger for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and for the Imam, and for the religion of the Muslims.'

key_terms.إِمَامٍ عَادِلٍ ظَاهِرٍ: Imam 'Adil Zahir: A Just, apparent/visible Imam (referring to the Imam in his visible role)
key_terms.الدِّيَة: Al-Diya: Blood money or compensation for killing
key_terms.بَيْتُ الْمَال: Bayt al-Mal: The public treasury of the Islamic state
key_terms.غَضَباً لِلَّهِ: Ghadaban lillah: Out of anger for the sake of Allah (religious zeal)
key_terms.نَصْب: Nasb: Hostility to the Imams, specifically the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for killing a Nasibi out of religious anger in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the distinction between ordinary judicial execution and the discretionary ruling of the Just Imam (al-Imam al-Adl), who exempts the killer from capital punishment due to his intent of 'ghadab lillah' (anger for God). It establishes that the diya is paid from the state treasury (bayt al-mal) rather than the killer's estate, reflecting the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt's enemies in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the Imam's authority to interpret the spirit of the law beyond strict retribution.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Bureyd Al Ajaly who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a Believer who kills a well-known Hostile one (Nasibi), upon his Religion, being angry for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High, would he be killed due to it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for them (rulers), so they would kill him for it, but if it were raised to a Just Imam<sup>asws</sup> present, he would not be killed for it’. 
I said, ‘So his blood would be invalidated’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but if there were inheritors for him, so it would be upon the Imam<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> gives them the wergild from the public treasury of the Muslims, because his killer, but rather his killing was an (act of) anger for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and for the Imam<sup>asws</sup>, and for the Religion of the Muslims’.
